1.w: My child, if you have made a pledge for your neighbor, if you have become a guarantor for a stranger,

2.w: if you have been ensnared by the words you have uttered and have been caught by the words you have spoken,

3.w: then, my child, do this in order to deliver yourself, because you have fallen into your neighbor’s power: Go, humble yourself, and appeal firmly to your neighbor.

4.w: Permit no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.

5.w: Deliver yourself like a gazelle from a snare and like a bird from the trap of the fowler.

6.w: Go to the ant, you sluggard; observe her ways and be wise!

7.w: It has no commander, overseer, or ruler,

8.w: yet it would prepare its food in the summer; it gathered at the harvest what it will eat.

9.w: How long, you sluggard, will you lie there? When will you rise from your sleep?

10.w: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to relax,

11.w: and your poverty will come like a robber, and your need like an armed man.

12.w: A worthless and wicked person walks around saying perverse things;

13.w: he winks with his eyes, signals with his feet, and points with his fingers;

14.w: he plots evil with perverse thoughts in his heart; he spreads contention at all times.

15.w: Therefore, his disaster will come suddenly; in an instant he will be broken, and there will be no remedy.

16.w: There are six things that the Lord hates, even seven things that are an abomination to him:

17.w: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

18.w: a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that are swift to run to evil,

19.w: a false witness who pours out lies, and a person who spreads discord among family members.

20.w: My child, guard the commands of your father and do not forsake the instruction of your mother.

21.w: Bind them on your heart continually; fasten them around your neck.

22.w: When you walk about, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; when you wake up, they will talk to you.

23.w: For the commandments are like a lamp; instruction is like a light, and rebukes of discipline are like the road leading to life

24.w: by keeping you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the loose woman.

25.w: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty, and do not let her captivate you with her alluring eyes;

26.w: for on account of a prostitute one is brought down to a loaf of bread, but the wife of another man preys on your precious life.

27.w: Can a man hold fire against his chest without burning his clothes?

28.w: Can a man walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?

29.w: So it is with the one who sleeps with his neighbor’s wife; no one who touches her will escape punishment.

30.w: People do not despise a thief when he steals to fulfill his need when he is hungry.

31.w: Yet if he is caught he must repay seven times over; he might even have to give all the wealth of his house.

32.w: A man who commits adultery with a woman lacks sense; whoever does it destroys his own life.

33.w: He will be beaten and despised, and his reproach will not be wiped away;

34.w: for jealousy kindles a husband’s rage, and he will not show mercy when he takes revenge.

35.w: He will not consider any compensation; he will not be willing, even if you multiply the compensation.
